notes:
Asserts working → waiting when a tool call opens Copilot's confirmation prompt. The signal is entirely transcript-borne — Copilot writes permission.requested to events.jsonl WHILE it sits blocked (CLI 1.0.77, kind=shell, hasWriteFileRedirection=true, held until teardown with NO permission.completed) — so no hook and no :7837 pinning is involved. That makes this cell replayable offline, unlike the hook-driven claudecode/codex siblings.

KNOWN_FAILING CLEARED 2026-08-03 (re-recorded green). The earlier recording of this cell was known_failing for a real daemon bug: session.MergeMetrics / newMergedMetrics (core/domain/session/metrics.go) did not copy TranscriptPermissionPending, and the LIVE detector classifies against the POST-merge state.Metrics, so the transcript_permission_prompt rule (state_classifier.go) read false on every pass and the session never left working. Replay was immune (replayengine feeds Convert output straight to the classifier), which is why the unit suites and replay-fixtures stayed green while live was broken. Fixed by commit "fix(session): carry TranscriptPermissionPending through MergeMetrics"; this re-recording shows the live daemon emitting state_transition new_state=waiting reason "transcript permission prompt open → waiting" with decided_by_tier=transcript / decided_by_rule=transcript_permission_prompt, so daemon_capability is back to full.

BIRTH SHAPE: the real session is born DIRECTLY into working, not ready. copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch with only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only when the first prompt is sent, so at discovery the file already holds the open turn and buildNewSessionState classifies the birth against its own metrics. The transient proc-<PID> row is still born ready and remains the presession anchor; session_birth and turn_start are ONE phase.

OBSERVATIONS assert `agent` only: the run terminates mid-turn with the prompt held, before any assistant.turn_end / session.usage_checkpoint / session.shutdown token block, so cost and tokens are legitimately zero here. Token/cost/model coverage belongs to 5-1_token-accounting and 5-2_model-identification.

copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd)

The write-class shell call has no matching approval rule, so Copilot writes permission.requested and blocks: TranscriptPermissionPending=true → transcript_permission_prompt → working → waiting, read from the transcript alone (no hook channel).

The waiting episode is user-visible and persists while the confirmation prompt is held — the recipe never answers it, so no permission.completed lands and the session does not slip to ready before teardown.
